en: I'm not sure; I don't really know

examples.en: I'm not sure about this word.

examples.ko: 죄송해요. 저도 이 동네는 잘 모르겠어요.
examples.en: Sorry, I don't really know this neighborhood either.

examples.ko: 이 약은 하루에 몇 번 먹어요? — 잘 모르겠어요.
examples.en: How many times a day do you take this medicine? — I'm not sure.

examples.ko: 오늘 저녁에 뭐 먹을까요? — 잘 모르겠어요. 뭐가 맛있어요?
examples.en: What shall we eat tonight? — I'm not sure. What's good?

examples.ko: 시험 문제가 너무 어려워요. 답을 잘 모르겠어요.
examples.en: The exam questions are so hard. I don't really know the answers.

explain: ‘잘 모르겠어요’는 ‘몰라요’보다 부드러워요. 확실하지 않을 때 써요. 친구에게 ‘몰라’라고만 하면 차갑게 들릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: 잘 모르겠어요 is softer than 몰라요. Use it when you are not sure. Just saying 몰라 to a friend can sound cold.

examples.en: I don't know that person's name.
I didn't know the way, so I looked at a map.
Do you know that singer? — No, I don't.
There are many words I don't know. I look in the dictionary.
I don't know that shop's phone number.

phrases.nuance_ko: 알면 오히려 마음이 아프니까 모르는 편이 낫다는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: a proverb: knowing can hurt more, so you are better off not knowing

국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: I don't understand what you mean.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 고향을 떠난 아들의 소식을 아무도 모른다.
dict_examples.en: Nobody knows any news of the son who left his hometown.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 모르다 becomes 몰라요, not 모르어요. 부르다 and 고르다 change the same way: 불러요, 골라요.

examples.en: I don't know what this word means.
I looked up the meaning of that word in the dictionary.
My name has a good meaning.

examples.ko: 이 말의 뜻을 영어로 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell me the meaning of this word in English.
I'm curious about the meaning of this song title.

explain: ‘뜻’은 말의 뜻도 되고 사람의 마음도 돼요. ‘그런 뜻이 아니에요’는 ‘그렇게 말하려고 한 게 아니에요’예요.

phrases.example: 우리는 뜻이 맞아서 같이 가게를 열었어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여기서 ‘뜻’은 말의 뜻이 아니라 생각이나 목표예요.
phrases.nuance_en: here 뜻 means a person's thoughts or goals, not the meaning of a word

dict_examples.ko: 모르는 낱말의 뜻을 알려면 사전을 찾아야 한다.
dict_examples.en: To know the meaning of an unfamiliar word, you have to look it up in a dictionary.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 네 뜻이 그렇다면 한번 해 봐라.
dict_examples.en: If that is what you want, then give it a try.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: I sincerely wish that you achieve your aspirations.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 아버지께서 말씀하신 뜻을 자식 된 도리로서 헤아리는 것은 당연하다.
dict_examples.en: It is only natural, as a child, to figure out the meaning of what one's father said.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 뜻 means the meaning of a word, and also what a person intends. 그런 뜻이 아니에요 means ‘I didn't mean it that way.’

examples.ko: 이 표시는 무슨 뜻이에요? 처음 봤어요.
examples.en: What does this mark mean? I've never seen it.

examples.ko: 화면에 빨간 점이 있어요. 무슨 뜻이에요?
examples.en: There's a red dot on the screen. What does it mean?

examples.ko: 이 표지판은 무슨 뜻이에요? — 여기에서 사진을 찍으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: What does this sign mean? — You can't take photos here.

examples.ko: 도로 위의 이 표지판은 무슨 뜻이에요?
examples.en: What does this sign on the road mean?
What does this button in the elevator mean?

explain: 모르는 말은 그 말을 먼저 말하고 물어요: ‘치맥이 무슨 뜻이에요?’ 친구에게는 ‘무슨 뜻이야?’라고 해요.
explain_en: Say the word you don't know first, then ask: 치맥이 무슨 뜻이에요? With friends, say 무슨 뜻이야?

examples.en: Teacher, how do you spell this word?
Sorry, how do I write the address?
How do you write your name in Hangul?

examples.ko: 이 신청서에 날짜를 어떻게 써요? — 숫자로 쓰세요.
examples.en: How do I write the date on this form? — Write it in numbers.
How do I write the address on this form?

explain: ‘쓰다’는 ‘써요’로 바뀌어요 (쓰어요 ✕). 같은 ‘쓰다’로 글을 쓰고, 모자를 쓰고, 돈을 써요.
explain_en: 쓰다 becomes 써요, not 쓰어요. The same verb means to write (글을 쓰다), to wear a hat (모자를 쓰다) and to spend money (돈을 쓰다).

examples.en: One moment. Let me check my notes.
Hold on, my wallet's gone.
Just a moment. I have a phone call.
Wait! I'm coming with you.

examples.ko: 여기요, 물 좀 주세요. — 네, 잠깐만요.
examples.en: Excuse me, some water please. — Yes, one moment.

explain_en: 잠깐만요 is shorter and softer than ‘please wait’. With friends, say 잠깐만.

examples.en: Ah, I get it now. Thank you.
Okay, now I get it.
I listened to the explanation twice and understood.

examples.ko: 이해했어요? — 아니요, 조금 더 설명해 주세요.
examples.en: Did you understand? — No, please explain a little more.
I understood this grammar by looking at the picture.

explain: 한국어는 ‘지금 알았다’고 말할 때 과거형 ‘이해했어요’를 써요. 같은 때 ‘알겠어요’도 많이 써요.
explain_en: Korean uses the past form 이해했어요 to say ‘I get it now’. 알겠어요 is also very common in the same situation.

examples.en: Teacher, I have a question.
After class there is question time.
Any questions? — Yes, I have one.
I sent my question by email.
That's a good question. One moment.

explain: ‘질문’은 사람에게 묻는 말이에요. 시험 문제는 ‘질문’이 아니라 ‘문제’라고 해요.

dict_examples.ko: 질문이 있으신 분은 발표가 끝난 후에 해 주시기 바랍니다.
dict_examples.en: Those who have questions, please ask after the presentation ends.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 질문 is a question you ask a person. A question on an exam is a 문제, not a 질문.

examples.en: Please answer the question.
I answered the teacher's question in Korean.
If you ask in Korean, I answer in Korean.
Please answer the email quickly.
The child doesn't answer even when I call his name.

dict_examples.ko: 그는 나에게 화가 났는지 내가 부르는 것에는 대답하지 않았다.
dict_examples.en: He may have been angry at me, as he did not answer when I called.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: Make sure to answer "yes" to adults.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: Say 질문에 대답해요, using 에. For a person, use 에게 or 한테.

examples.ko: 토요일 오후 네 시, 2번 출구 앞. 이거 맞아요?
examples.en: Saturday, 4 p.m., in front of Exit 2. Is that right?
I wrote down my address. Is this right?
I did my homework. Is this right?
Is this right? — Yes, you wrote it well.
I bought a train ticket. Is this the right one?

explain: 내가 한 것이나 고른 것을 보여 주면서 확인할 때 써요. 말만 확인할 때는 그냥 ‘맞아요?’라고 해요.
explain_en: Use it when you show something you did or chose and want it checked. To check only what someone said, just ask 맞아요?

examples.en: Is it Saturday? — Yes, that's right.

examples.ko: 이 버스 강남역에 가요? — 네, 맞아요.
examples.en: Does this bus go to Gangnam Station? — Yes, it does.

examples.ko: 부산에서 오셨어요? — 네, 맞아요. 부산 사람이에요.
examples.en: Did you come from Busan? — Yes, that's right. I'm from Busan.
The exam is tomorrow, right? — Yes, that's right.

examples.ko: 길이 이쪽이에요? — 네, 맞아요. 쭉 가세요.
examples.en: Is the way this direction? — Yes, that's right. Go straight.

explain: 상대 말에 ‘저도 그래요’라는 마음으로도 ‘맞아요’라고 해요. 친구에게는 ‘맞아’라고 해요.
explain_en: 맞아요 is also used to agree: ‘you're right, me too.’ With friends, say 맞아.

examples.ko: 세 시예요? — 아니요, 아니에요. 네 시예요.
examples.en: Is it three? — No, it's not. It's four.
Is this coffee? — No, it isn't. It's green tea.
Are you tired? — No, I'm not. I'm fine.
I'm sorry. — No, no. It's fine.

examples.ko: 저 사람이 사장이에요? — 아니요, 아니에요. 직원이에요.
examples.en: Is that person the boss? — No, he isn't. He's an employee.

explain: ‘고마워요’나 ‘미안해요’라는 말에 ‘아니에요’라고 대답할 수도 있어요. ‘괜찮아요, 별일 아니에요’라는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: You can also answer ‘thank you’ or ‘sorry’ with 아니에요, meaning ‘it's nothing, don't worry’.

examples.en: Sorry, I didn't quite hear that.
I'm sorry. I don't have time right now.

explain: '미안해요'보다 더 공손해서 윗사람, 손님, 처음 만난 사람에게 써요. 회의나 가게처럼 격식 있는 자리에서는 '죄송합니다'가 더 자연스러워요. 부탁하거나 말을 걸 때 '죄송한데요'로 시작하면 부드럽게 들려요.

dict_examples.en: Sorry I'm late. The traffic was really bad.
I'm really sorry to have kept you waiting.

dict_examples.ko: 죄송해요, 그 물건은 지금 다 팔렸어요.
dict_examples.en: I'm sorry, that item is sold out right now.

explain_en: It is more polite than '미안해요', so use it with elders, customers and people you've just met. In formal settings like meetings or shops, '죄송합니다' sounds more natural. Starting a request with '죄송한데요' makes it sound softer.
